result.summary: For each n, restrict to the open dense class of symmetric matrices having simple spectrum, every nonempty principal minor nonzero, and every physical off-diagonal coefficient nonzero. If a universal interval-density constant C is proved uniformly on this class with strict target margin s_3>1, then the identical C holds for every target matrix with s_3>=1. Proof uses scaling to (1+eta)A, operator-norm generic approximation, samplewise quadratic convergence with no moment bound, buffered intervals/Fatou, then eta->0. In parallel, arbitrary cap-one source laws are approximated in L1 by smooth compact strict-subcap one-interval-positive densities via tail-mass relocation, mollification and an arbitrarily small broad bridge; tensor TV and pushforward contraction preserve exactly C. Thus the full essential-height target is equivalent, at the level of a uniform constant, to the smooth-connected-source/generic-strict-matrix core. Continuity does not pass through this closure.

partner_dependency.used_inequality: If a physical 3x3 principal block B has sigma=min|lambda(B)|>0 then ||p_(X^TAX)||_(infinity,ess)<=6sqrt(pi)/sigma.
partner_dependency.actual_application: Applied to generic approximants G_k of (1+eta)A. Their selected block scales sigma_k converge to (1+eta)sigma, so r10 gives 6sqrt(pi)/sigma_k; buffered-interval passage and output rescaling recover exactly 6sqrt(pi)/sigma with no closure loss.

scope_guard: Genericization removes exact algebraic degeneracies only. It gives no universal positive lower bound on any nonzero physical pivot, principal minor, Schur complement determinant, spectral margin above one, connected-support bridge floor, or support diameter. Any proof that pays bare reciprocal degeneracy remains non-uniform.
next_action: Use the generic strict core to derive a Schur/elimination identity where reciprocal small pivots are compensated by aggregate product-projection or cross-volume resources before conditioning destroys product provenance.
